newsitem.title: USA: Genzyme says FDA okays Cerezyme plant.
newsitem.headline: Genzyme says FDA okays Cerezyme plant.

text.p: Genzyme Corp said on Thursday the Food and Drug Administration had granted approval for the company to manufacture its drug Cerezyme in the new Allston Landing plant in Boston.

The company said it plans to start distributing Cerezyme from the Allston plant to some customers in the United States by the end of 1996. It is completing reports on validation of the manufacturing process for submission to the FDA's New England District Office.
Cerezyme is a recombinant version of Ceredase, Genzyme's tissue-derived enzyme-replacement product.
Ceredase and Cerezyme are the only approved products indicated for type I Gaucher disease.

Genzyme received FDA approval to market Cerezyme from a smaller plant in May 1994. Since then, the company has been able to supply a small number of patients with the product, while supplying the rest with Ceredase.
